name: Hearthstone Firearms Defender-38 'Snubnose'
description:
The Hearthstone Defender-38 is a five-shot double-action revolver chambered in .38 Special with a two-inch barrel, designed as the ultimate simple defensive weapon. The frame is aluminum alloy to reduce weight, the hammer is shrouded to prevent snagging on clothing during draw, and there is no adjustable sight — just a milled groove in the top strap that serves as a rudimentary sight channel.

The Snubnose is the revolver equivalent of the Guardian-12 — a weapon for people who want something simple, safe, and effective at arm's length. The two-inch barrel makes it genuinely pocketable, and the shrouded hammer allows a smooth draw from a coat pocket without catching on fabric. Five rounds of .38 Special won't win a prolonged firefight, but at the ranges where this weapon will be used — typically less than three meters — the point is to survive the first ten seconds.

Hearthstone sells the Defender-38 with a soft fabric pocket holster and a five-round speedloader. Their marketing is characteristically practical: 'Five answers to one question.' The weapon sells steadily across all tiers, from Shelf grandmothers who keep one in their housecoat pocket to Mid executives who slip one into their overcoat as a deep-concealment backup.

tactical_use: A minimal defensive revolver for close-range emergency use. The shrouded hammer enables snag-free pocket draw. Five rounds of .38 Special provide adequate close-range stopping power against unarmored targets. Not accurate beyond conversational distance. Designed to be drawn and fired at contact range during surprise encounters.
cultural_context: The Snubnose crosses all social boundaries. It is the one firearm that Shelf residents and Mid executives carry for the same reason in the same way — tucked in a pocket, available instantly, hopefully never needed. Its universal presence is a quiet commentary on the baseline anxiety that pervades all tiers of GLMZ.
story_hooks: A dying person hands a Snubnose to a stranger with the words 'Keep this safe' — the weapon contains a microdrive embedded in the grip that holds information worth killing for.
A trend of decorating Snubnoses with personalized grip panels becomes popular in Mid social circles, turning a weapon of anxiety into a fashion accessory.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, rounded revolver with a distinctly stubby profile. The shrouded hammer creates a smooth, bulbous crown at the rear. The short barrel gives it an almost toy-like appearance until you notice the serious muzzle and the weight-forward balance of the cylinder. It reads as 'practical' rather than intimidating — a working-class tool, not a showpiece.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 16.5 cm, cylinder diameter 4.2 cm, barrel length 5 cm, grip height 10 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Light and balanced — the aluminum frame keeps it featherweight (380g), distributing mass evenly between grip and cylinder. Feels responsive in the hand, not front-heavy despite the compact proportions.
physical_description.primary_material: Aluminum alloy frame, steel cylinder and barrel, polymer grip panels
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray on frame, dark blued steel on cylinder and barrel. The shrouded hammer features a slightly brushed nickel accent. Worn in typical field units with minor scuffs and handling marks.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray with dark blue-black steel accents, charcoal polymer grip panels
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with shallow grip lines for purchase — nothing fancy, designed for quick acquisition from a coat pocket. Slightly tacky feel, worn smooth in high-contact areas.
distinctive_features: Shrouded hammer — smooth rounded profile with no exposed spur
Milled sight groove in top strap — functional minimalism
Five-shot cylinder with visible round heads
Stubby 5cm barrel with sharp muzzle crown
Cylinder release button integrated flush with frame
No adjustable sights or accessory rail
Minor holster wear on frame edges and grip panels
Faint factory rust preventative patina on steel
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HEARTHSTONE FIREARMS stamped in serif font on left frame above trigger guard. DEFENDER-38 model designation micro-etched on barrel. Serial number on bottom of frame near cylinder pin. Caliber marking (.38 SPECIAL) on cylinder top strap. Minimal branding — strictly functional.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but battle-worn. Shows the patina of frequent carry and use — light holster rubs, slight cylinder-to-frame play from regular use, but mechanically sound. Kept functional rather than pristine.
